title: Chicken Karahi
description: A rich, aromatic tomato-based chicken dish cooked in a traditional wok-style karahi with ginger, garlic, and green chilies.

instructions.title: Sear the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed karahi or wok over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces and sear for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly browned on all sides.

instructions.title: Build the base
instructions.instruction: Add sliced onion and cumin seeds. Cook for 4-5 minutes until the onion softens and turns translucent.

instructions.title: Add aromatics
instructions.instruction: Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly to prevent burning.

instructions.title: Cook the tomatoes
instructions.instruction: Add chopped tomatoes, red chili powder, and salt. Cook for 10-12 minutes, mashing occasionally, until the tomatoes break down into a thick, oil-separated masala.

instructions.title: Simmer the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add green chilies, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Finish and garnish
instructions.instruction: Uncover, increase heat briefly to thicken the sauce if needed, then remove from heat. Garnish with julienned ginger and fresh coriander.

tips: Use bone-in chicken for deeper flavor in the gravy.
For an authentic finish, add a splash of water and a knob of butter at the very end for gloss.

substitutions.effect: Slightly sweeter, smoother sauce with less texture than fresh tomatoes.

storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with naan or steamed basmati rice and a side of raita.

title: Chicken Biryani
description: Fragrant basmati rice layered with spiced marinated chicken, caramelized onions, and saffron, slow-cooked to perfection.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Combine chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, and salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes (longer improves flavor).

instructions.title: Par-cook the rice
instructions.instruction: Boil water with whole spices and salt. Add soaked basmati rice and cook until 70% done (still firm at the core). Drain and set aside.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken masala
instructions.instruction: Heat oil, sauté chopped tomatoes and half the fried onions for 5 minutes, then add the marinated chicken. Cook covered for 20-25 minutes until chicken is tender and the gravy thickens.

instructions.title: Layer the biryani
instructions.instruction: In a heavy pot, spread the chicken masala as the base layer, then top evenly with the par-cooked rice. Sprinkle remaining fried onions, mint, coriander, and saffron milk over the top.

instructions.title: Dum cook
instructions.instruction: Cover tightly with a lid (seal with dough or foil if needed) and cook on very low heat for 20-25 minutes to let the flavors steam through.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Turn off the heat and let the biryani rest, covered, for 10 minutes before gently fluffing and serving.

tips: Soak the rice for 30 minutes before cooking for longer, fluffier grains.
Don't skip the resting step — it lets the layers finish steaming evenly.

substitutions.substitute: A pinch of turmeric in the milk
substitutions.effect: Loses saffron's floral aroma but still gives a warm golden color.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat with a splash of water, covered, over low heat.
serving_suggestions: Serve with raita, salad, and boiled eggs.

title: Daal Chawal (Yellow Lentils & Rice)
description: A comforting, budget-friendly staple of spiced yellow lentils served over fluffy steamed rice.

ingredients.item: Yellow split lentils (chana daal or masoor)

instructions.title: Cook the lentils
instructions.instruction: Rinse lentils and boil in 700ml water with turmeric and salt for 20-25 minutes until soft and starting to break down.

instructions.title: Cook the rice
instructions.instruction: Simultaneously, rinse rice and cook in a separate pot with salted water until fluffy and fully cooked.

instructions.title: Prepare the tarka
instructions.instruction: In a small pan, heat oil and cumin seeds until they sizzle, then add garlic and onion. Fry for 4-5 minutes until golden.

instructions.title: Finish the daal
instructions.instruction: Add chopped tomato and red chili powder to the tarka, cook for 3 minutes until softened, then pour the entire tarka over the cooked lentils and stir to combine.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Simmer the daal for 2 more minutes to marry the flavors, then serve hot over steamed rice.

tips: Mash some of the lentils against the pot for a creamier texture.
A final tarka of hot oil, garlic, and dried red chili on top adds restaurant-style flavor.

substitutions.effect: Cooks faster and gives a softer, creamier texture with a milder flavor.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freezes well for up to 2 months.
serving_suggestions: Serve with a wedge of lemon, sliced onion, and green chilies.

title: Garlic Naan
description: Soft, pillowy leavened flatbread brushed with garlic butter and baked until blistered and golden.

instructions.title: Activate the yeast
instructions.instruction: Dissolve sugar and yeast in warm water. Let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.

instructions.title: Make the dough
instructions.instruction: Combine flour, salt, yogurt, and the yeast mixture. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.

instructions.title: Let it rise
instructions.instruction: Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape and cook
instructions.instruction: Divide into 6 balls, roll each into an oval, and cook on a very hot skillet or in a hot oven (250°C) until puffed and charred in spots.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Brush hot naan immediately with garlic butter and sprinkle with fresh coriander.

tips: A cast-iron skillet gets closest to tandoor-style char at home.
Keep naan covered with a cloth after cooking to stay soft.

substitutions.effect: Slightly less tang and a marginally less tender crumb.

storage: Store in an airtight bag at room temperature for 1 day, or freeze for up to 1 month.
serving_suggestions: Perfect alongside karahi, curries, or daal.

title: Mango Lassi
description: A refreshing, creamy yogurt-based drink blended with sweet ripe mango and a hint of cardamom.

instructions.title: Blend
instructions.instruction: Combine mango, yogurt, milk, sugar, and cardamom powder in a blender.

instructions.title: Add ice and blend again
instructions.instruction: Add ice cubes and blend until smooth and frothy.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Pour into glasses and serve immediately, garnished with a mint leaf if desired.

tips: Use frozen mango chunks for an extra-thick, milkshake-like texture without needing much ice.

substitutions.effect: Adds a subtle coconut note and makes the drink dairy-free.

storage: Best served fresh; can be refrigerated for up to 1 day in a sealed container.
serving_suggestions: Great alongside spicy dishes like karahi or biryani to balance the heat.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
description: Tender tandoori-spiced chicken simmered in a velvety, mildly spiced tomato-butter-cream sauce.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Mix chicken with yogurt, tandoori masala, and half the ginger-garlic paste. Marinate at least 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Sear the chicken
instructions.instruction: Sear the marinated chicken in a hot pan with 1 tbsp butter for 5-6 minutes until browned but not fully cooked through. Set aside.

instructions.title: Build the sauce
instructions.instruction: In the same pan, melt remaining butter, add remaining ginger-garlic paste, and cook 1 minute. Add tomato puree, chili powder, and sugar. Simmer for 12-15 minutes until thickened and the raw tomato smell is gone.

instructions.title: Combine and finish
instructions.instruction: Stir in cream and garam masala, then return the chicken to the pan. Simmer for 8-10 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and the sauce coats it thickly.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove from heat, stir in a final knob of butter, and garnish with fresh coriander.

tips: Blending the sauce before adding cream gives an ultra-smooth restaurant texture.
Kashmiri chili powder gives color without excessive heat.

substitutions.substitute: Cashew paste (soaked cashews blended with water)
substitutions.effect: Slightly nuttier flavor and a bit lighter, still creamy.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freezes well for up to 2 months.
serving_suggestions: Serve with garlic naan or steamed basmati rice.

title: Masala Dosa
description: A crisp, golden fermented rice-and-lentil crepe filled with a spiced potato masala, a South Indian breakfast classic.

instructions.title: Make the potato masala
instructions.instruction: Heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves until they crackle. Add onion and green chilies, cook 4-5 minutes until soft.

instructions.title: Finish the masala
instructions.instruction: Add turmeric and boiled potatoes, mash lightly, season with salt, and cook 5 minutes, stirring to combine. Keep warm.

instructions.title: Heat the pan
instructions.instruction: Heat a flat non-stick or cast-iron griddle and lightly grease it.

instructions.title: Spread the batter
instructions.instruction: Pour a ladle of dosa batter in the center and spread outward in a thin, even circular motion using the back of the ladle.

instructions.title: Cook until crisp
instructions.instruction: Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until the underside is golden and crisp, about 2-3 minutes. Do not flip.

instructions.title: Fill and fold
instructions.instruction: Place a portion of potato masala in the center, fold the dosa over, and serve immediately.

tips: A well-fermented, slightly sour batter is key to authentic flavor.
Keep the griddle consistently hot for even crisping.

substitutions.effect: Saves time; flavor is close but slightly less tangy than home-fermented batter.

storage: Batter keeps refrigerated up to 3 days; cooked dosa is best fresh.
serving_suggestions: Serve with coconut chutney and sambar.

title: Vegetable Fried Rice
description: A quick, wok-tossed fried rice loaded with crisp vegetables, garlic, and soy sauce — ready in under 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Scramble the eggs
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a hot wok, pour in beaten eggs, scramble quickly, and set aside.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add remaining oil, then garlic, carrot, and bell pepper. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until just tender-crisp.

instructions.title: Add the rice
instructions.instruction: Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps with a spatula, and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until heated through and starting to crisp slightly.

instructions.title: Season
instructions.instruction: Add peas, scrambled eggs, soy sauce, white pepper, and half the spring onion. Toss everything together for 2 minutes.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Drizzle sesame oil, toss once more, and garnish with remaining spring onion before serving.

tips: Day-old, chilled rice fries up far less mushy than freshly cooked rice.
Keep the wok very hot throughout for that signature 'wok hei' flavor.

substitutions.effect: Makes the dish vegan; slightly less rich but still satisfying protein.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat in a hot pan or microwave.
serving_suggestions: Pairs well with chili oil or a side of spring rolls.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: A bold Sichuan stir-fry of diced chicken, roasted peanuts, and dried chilies in a tangy-sweet-savory sauce.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Toss diced chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp cornstarch. Let sit for 10 minutes.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, and remaining cornstarch with 3 tbsp water. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sear the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a wok over high heat, add chicken, and stir-fry until golden and cooked through, about 5-6 minutes. Remove and set aside.

instructions.title: Toast the aromatics
instructions.instruction: In the same wok, add dried chilies, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry for 30-60 seconds until fragrant (careful not to burn).

instructions.title: Combine and finish
instructions.instruction: Return chicken to the wok, pour in the sauce, and toss until it thickens and coats everything, about 2 minutes. Stir in peanuts and spring onion just before serving.

tips: Toast the peanuts lightly beforehand for extra crunch and flavor.
Adjust dried chilies for your preferred spice level.

substitutions.effect: Milder, slightly sweeter crunch — also useful for peanut allergies.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
serving_suggestions: Serve over steamed jasmine rice.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
description: Pan-seared chicken thighs glazed in a glossy, sweet-savory soy-mirin sauce, a Japanese home-cooking staple.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, garlic, and ginger in a small bowl.

instructions.title: Sear the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down and cook for 6-7 minutes until deeply golden.

instructions.title: Flip and cook through
instructions.instruction: Flip and cook the other side for 5-6 minutes until nearly cooked through.

instructions.title: Glaze
instructions.instruction: Pour the sauce over the chicken, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer, spooning sauce over the chicken, for 5-6 minutes until it thickens into a glossy glaze and chicken is cooked through (internal temp 74°C/165°F).

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Rest for 3 minutes, slice, and spoon remaining glaze over. Garnish with sesame seeds and spring onion.

tips: Let the sauce reduce slowly for a proper glaze — rushing on high heat can burn the sugars.
Chicken thighs stay juicier than breast for this method.

substitutions.effect: Slightly less complex sweetness but a very close substitute.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed rice and steamed broccoli or edamame.

title: Miso Soup
description: A delicate, umami-rich soup of dashi broth, miso paste, silken tofu, and wakame seaweed.

instructions.title: Rehydrate wakame
instructions.instruction: Soak dried wakame in water for 5 minutes until softened, then drain.

instructions.title: Heat the dashi
instructions.instruction: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer in a pot — do not let it boil hard.

instructions.title: Dissolve the miso
instructions.instruction: Ladle a little hot dashi into a small bowl, whisk in miso paste until smooth, then stir it back into the pot.

instructions.title: Add tofu and wakame
instructions.instruction: Gently add tofu cubes and wakame, and warm through for 2-3 minutes without boiling (boiling dulls the miso flavor).

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle into bowls and garnish with spring onion.

tips: Never boil miso soup vigorously — it destroys the delicate flavor and beneficial cultures in the miso.
Add miso at the very end for the freshest taste.

substitutions.effect: Loses the distinct smoky-umami dashi note but keeps the soup vegetarian-friendly.

storage: Best fresh; refrigerate up to 1 day (tofu texture softens on reheating).
serving_suggestions: A classic starter alongside sushi, teriyaki, or a rice bowl.

title: Bibimbap
description: A vibrant Korean rice bowl topped with seasoned sautéed vegetables, marinated beef, a fried egg, and spicy gochujang sauce.

instructions.title: Marinate the beef
instructions.instruction: Toss beef slices with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, and half the garlic. Marinate 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Blanch and season spinach
instructions.instruction: Blanch spinach for 30 seconds, drain, squeeze out water, and toss with a little sesame oil, garlic, and salt.

instructions.title: Sauté each vegetable separately
instructions.instruction: Quickly sauté carrot, zucchini, bean sprouts, and mushrooms individually for 2-3 minutes each, seasoning lightly with salt and sesame oil, keeping them separate.

instructions.title: Cook the beef
instructions.instruction: Stir-fry the marinated beef in a hot pan for 3-4 minutes until browned and cooked through.

instructions.title: Fry the eggs
instructions.instruction: Fry eggs sunny-side up in a separate pan, keeping yolks runny.

instructions.title: Assemble
instructions.instruction: Divide rice among bowls, arrange vegetables, beef, and a fried egg on top in sections. Serve with gochujang and sesame seeds, mixing everything together just before eating.

tips: Cook each vegetable separately to preserve distinct textures and flavors.
Mix vigorously right before eating so every bite gets a bit of everything.

substitutions.effect: Makes the dish vegetarian with a similar savory-marinated bite, though less rich.

storage: Best fresh; store components separately in the fridge for up to 2 days.
serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of kimchi.

title: Kimchi Fried Rice
description: A punchy, quick weeknight fried rice built around tangy fermented kimchi and topped with a fried egg.

instructions.title: Sauté kimchi
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a pan, add garlic and kimchi, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly caramelized.

instructions.title: Add rice
instructions.instruction: Add rice, kimchi juice, gochujang, and soy sauce. Break up clumps and stir-fry for 5-6 minutes until well combined and slightly crisp in spots.

instructions.title: Fry the eggs
instructions.instruction: In a separate pan, fry eggs sunny-side up with crispy edges.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Drizzle sesame oil over the rice, top each portion with a fried egg, sesame seeds, and spring onion.

tips: Well-fermented, slightly sour kimchi gives the best depth of flavor.
A runny yolk mixed in at the table makes the dish extra rich.

substitutions.effect: Makes the dish vegan while still adding protein and texture contrast.

storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
serving_suggestions: Great with a side of steamed dumplings.

title: Thai Green Curry Chicken
description: Fragrant coconut curry simmered with green curry paste, tender chicken, Thai basil, and vegetables.

instructions.title: Fry the curry paste
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the green curry paste for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add coconut milk
instructions.instruction: Pour in half the coconut milk, stirring to combine with the paste, and simmer for 3-4 minutes until it starts to separate slightly (this deepens the flavor).

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add chicken slices and cook for 5-6 minutes until mostly cooked through, stirring to coat in the sauce.

instructions.title: Add vegetables and remaining liquid
instructions.instruction: Stir in remaining coconut milk, eggplant/zucchini, bell pepper, fish sauce, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until vegetables are tender and chicken is fully cooked.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Remove from heat, stir in Thai basil and sliced chili just before serving.

tips: Frying the curry paste in oil first (not directly in coconut milk) builds much deeper flavor.
Add fresh herbs at the very end so they stay vibrant.

substitutions.substitute: Soy sauce + a squeeze of lime
substitutions.effect: Milder umami and no fish flavor, suitable for pescatarian-avoidant diets, though less traditional.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; coconut curries also freeze reasonably well.
serving_suggestions: Serve over jasmine rice.

title: Pad Thai
description: Stir-fried rice noodles with shrimp or chicken, egg, tofu, bean sprouts, and a signature sweet-tangy tamarind sauce.

instructions.title: Soak the noodles
instructions.instruction: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 20-25 minutes until pliable but still firm. Drain.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar until dissolved. Set aside.

instructions.title: Stir-fry protein and tofu
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a wok, add garlic, then shrimp/chicken and tofu. Cook for 3-4 minutes until nearly done. Push to one side.

instructions.title: Scramble the egg
instructions.instruction: Crack eggs into the empty side of the wok and scramble briefly, then mix with the protein.

instructions.title: Add noodles and sauce
instructions.instruction: Add drained noodles and the sauce mixture. Toss continuously for 4-5 minutes until noodles are tender and evenly coated.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Add bean sprouts and half the peanuts, toss for 1 more minute, then remove from heat. Top with remaining peanuts, spring onion, and serve with lime wedges.

tips: Don't over-soak the noodles — they'll finish cooking in the wok and can turn mushy.
Keep the wok hot and keep tossing to avoid clumping.

substitutions.substitute: Lime juice + a touch of brown sugar
substitutions.effect: Brighter, more purely sour flavor without tamarind's fruity depth.

storage: Best fresh; refrigerate up to 2 days, though noodles firm up on reheating.
serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges and chili flakes on the side.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: A deceptively simple Roman classic: spaghetti tossed in garlic-infused olive oil, chili flakes, and parsley.

instructions.title: Boil the pasta
instructions.instruction: Cook spaghetti in generously salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining.

instructions.title: Infuse the oil
instructions.instruction: While pasta cooks, gently heat olive oil in a large pan over low-medium heat. Add sliced garlic and cook slowly for 3-4 minutes until golden and fragrant — do not let it brown or burn.

instructions.title: Add chili
instructions.instruction: Add chili flakes to the oil and cook for 30 seconds more.

instructions.title: Combine
instructions.instruction: Add drained pasta directly to the pan along with a splash of reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously for 1-2 minutes until the sauce clings to the noodles and turns glossy.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Remove from heat, stir in parsley, and season with salt to taste. Top with Parmesan if desired.

tips: Burnt garlic turns bitter — keep the heat low and watch it closely.
The starchy pasta water is what makes the sauce silky, not just oil.

substitutions.effect: Makes the dish vegan with a similar savory, slightly cheesy note.

storage: Best fresh; refrigerate up to 2 days, adding a splash of olive oil when reheating.
serving_suggestions: A simple side salad and crusty bread round out the meal.

title: Margherita Pizza
description: Classic Neapolitan-style pizza with a crisp-chewy crust, San Marzano tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and basil.

instructions.title: Prepare the sauce
instructions.instruction: Mix crushed tomatoes with garlic, a pinch of salt, and 1 tbsp olive oil. Do not cook — it cooks in the oven.

instructions.title: Preheat
instructions.instruction: Preheat your oven as high as it goes (250-280°C) with a pizza stone or heavy baking sheet inside for at least 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape the dough
instructions.instruction: On a floured surface, stretch the dough into a 12-inch round, leaving a slightly thicker rim for the crust.

instructions.title: Top the pizza
instructions.instruction: Spread the tomato sauce evenly, leaving the rim bare. Distribute torn mozzarella evenly across the top.

instructions.title: Bake
instructions.instruction: Carefully transfer the pizza onto the hot stone/sheet and bake for 8-12 minutes until the crust is puffed and golden with leopard-spotted char, and the cheese is bubbling.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Remove from the oven, drizzle with remaining olive oil, and scatter fresh basil leaves on top before slicing.

tips: A screaming-hot oven is essential — home ovens rarely match a pizza oven, so preheat as long as possible.
Add basil after baking so it stays bright and fragrant instead of wilting.

substitutions.effect: Less creamy pull and slightly more browning, but more convenient and less watery.

equipment: Pizza stone or heavy baking sheet
storage: Best fresh; leftovers keep refrigerated 2 days, reheat in a hot pan or oven.
serving_suggestions: Pair with a simple arugula salad dressed in lemon and olive oil.

title: Tiramisu
description: A no-bake Italian dessert of espresso-soaked ladyfingers layered with a silky mascarpone cream, dusted with cocoa.

instructions.title: Whisk yolks and sugar
instructions.instruction: Whisk egg yolks and sugar together over a double boiler (or use a stand mixer) until pale, thick, and doubled in volume, about 5-8 minutes.

instructions.title: Fold in mascarpone
instructions.instruction: Remove from heat and gently fold in mascarpone until smooth and no lumps remain.

instructions.title: Whip the cream
instructions.instruction: In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks, then gently fold into the mascarpone mixture.

instructions.title: Soak the ladyfingers
instructions.instruction: Mix cooled espresso with coffee liqueur if using. Quickly dip each ladyfinger for 1-2 seconds per side (don't oversoak, or they'll turn mushy) and layer in a dish.

instructions.title: Layer
instructions.instruction: Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers. Repeat with a second layer of soaked ladyfingers and remaining cream.

instructions.title: Chill and finish
instructions.instruction: Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (overnight is best) to set. Dust generously with cocoa powder just before serving.

tips: Use raw or very lightly cooked egg yolks with caution — a double-boiler method reduces raw-egg risk.
Chilling overnight gives the best texture as the layers meld together.

substitutions.substitute: Pasteurized egg yolks or a stabilized custard base
substitutions.effect: Removes raw-egg food safety concerns with only a very minor difference in richness.

storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days.
serving_suggestions: Serve chilled with a small espresso on the side.

title: Chicken Street Tacos
description: Charred, spice-marinated chicken tucked into warm corn tortillas with onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Combine chicken with lime juice, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, olive oil, and salt. Marinate for at least 20 minutes, ideally 1-2 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Grill or pan-sear the chicken over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until charred spots form and internal temperature reaches 74°C/165°F.

instructions.title: Rest and chop
instructions.instruction: Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then chop or shred into bite-sized pieces.

instructions.title: Warm the tortillas
instructions.instruction: Warm corn tortillas directly over a flame or in a dry skillet for 20-30 seconds per side until pliable and lightly toasted.

instructions.title: Assemble
instructions.instruction: Fill each tortilla with chopped chicken, diced onion, and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

tips: Doubling up corn tortillas prevents them from tearing under juicy fillings.
A hot cast-iron pan gives good char without a grill.

substitutions.effect: Makes the tacos vegetarian with a similarly juicy, meaty texture.

storage: Refrigerate components separately up to 3 days; assemble fresh.
serving_suggestions: Serve with salsa verde and a cold horchata.

title: Guacamole
description: A fresh, chunky avocado dip brightened with lime, cilantro, onion, and jalapeño.

instructions.title: Mash the avocado
instructions.instruction: Halve and pit avocados, scoop the flesh into a bowl, and mash to your preferred texture (chunky or smooth) with a fork.

instructions.title: Add lime immediately
instructions.instruction: Stir in lime juice right away to prevent browning and add brightness.

instructions.title: Combine
instructions.instruction: Fold in onion, tomato, jalapeño, cilantro, and garlic until evenly distributed.

instructions.title: Season and rest
instructions.instruction: Season with salt to taste. Let sit for 5-10 minutes for the flavors to meld before serving.

tips: Press plastic wrap directly onto the surface if storing to slow browning.
Adding the avocado pit to the bowl is a folk remedy — lime juice and airtight storage matter more.

substitutions.effect: Adds heat without the fresh pepper's grassy flavor and crunch.

storage: Best fresh; refrigerate with plastic wrap pressed on the surface for up to 1 day.
serving_suggestions: Serve with tortilla chips or as a taco topping.

title: Chicken Shish Kebab
description: Skewered chicken marinated in yogurt, garlic, and Turkish spices, grilled until smoky and juicy.

instructions.title: Marinate
instructions.instruction: Combine chicken with yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, paprika, cumin, pepper paste, olive oil, and salt. Marinate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.

instructions.title: Skewer
instructions.instruction: Thread marinated chicken onto skewers, alternating with bell pepper and onion chunks.

instructions.title: Preheat the grill
instructions.instruction: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.

instructions.title: Grill the skewers
instructions.instruction: Grill for 12-15 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes, until chicken is charred in spots and cooked through (internal temp 74°C/165°F).

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Rest for 3 minutes before serving.

tips: Yogurt-based marinades tenderize chicken beautifully — don't skip the marinating time.
Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes beforehand to prevent burning.

substitutions.effect: More forgiving and juicier on the grill, slightly higher in fat.

storage: Refrigerate marinated raw chicken up to 1 day; cooked leftovers up to 3 days.
serving_suggestions: Serve with rice pilaf, grilled tomatoes, and a side of garlic yogurt sauce.

title: Classic Hummus
description: A silky, creamy chickpea and tahini dip brightened with lemon, garlic, and olive oil.

instructions.title: Blend tahini and lemon
instructions.instruction: Blend tahini and lemon juice together first for 1 minute until pale and creamy — this step is key to a smooth final texture.

instructions.title: Add remaining ingredients
instructions.instruction: Add chickpeas, garlic, cumin, and salt. Blend for 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides.

instructions.title: Adjust texture
instructions.instruction: With the blender running, drizzle in olive oil and ice-cold water gradually until the hummus reaches a light, whippy consistency.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Spread onto a plate, drizzle with more olive oil, and dust with paprika.

tips: Blending tahini and lemon before adding chickpeas is the trick to ultra-smooth hummus.
Ice-cold water helps whip air into the mixture for a lighter texture.

substitutions.effect: Different but pleasant nutty flavor; not traditional and adds allergen risk for nut allergies.

storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 5 days.
serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread and fresh vegetable sticks.

title: Classic Cheeseburger
description: A juicy, griddle-seared beef patty topped with melted cheddar, lettuce, tomato, and a toasted bun.

instructions.title: Form the patties
instructions.instruction: Divide beef into 4 equal portions and gently shape into patties slightly wider than the buns (they shrink while cooking). Press a small dimple in the center of each. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper.

instructions.title: Toast the buns
instructions.instruction: Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast in a hot pan for 1 minute until golden. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sear the patties
instructions.instruction: Heat the same pan or griddle over high heat. Cook patties for 3 minutes without pressing down, until a deep crust forms.

instructions.title: Flip and add cheese
instructions.instruction: Flip patties, immediately top with cheese, and cook for 2-3 more minutes until cheese melts and internal temperature reaches at least 71°C/160°F for safety.

instructions.title: Assemble
instructions.instruction: Build each burger: bottom bun, lettuce, patty with melted cheese, tomato, onion, pickles, top bun.

tips: Don't press down on the patty while it cooks — it squeezes out the juices.
80/20 ground beef gives the best balance of flavor and juiciness.

substitutions.effect: Makes the burger vegetarian/vegan-friendly with a similar texture, milder savory flavor.

storage: Best fresh; store cooked patties separately from buns/toppings for up to 2 days.
serving_suggestions: Serve with crispy fries and a cold soda.

title: Classic Fluffy Pancakes
description: Light, fluffy buttermilk pancakes with crisp golden edges, perfect with maple syrup and butter.

instructions.title: Mix dry ingredients
instructions.instruction: Whisk together flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.

instructions.title: Mix wet ingredients
instructions.instruction: In a separate bowl, whisk milk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.

instructions.title: Combine
instructions.instruction: Pour wet ingredients into dry and whisk just until combined — a few small lumps are fine. Overmixing makes pancakes tough.

instructions.title: Rest the batter
instructions.instruction: Let the batter rest for 5 minutes; this lets the baking powder activate and gluten relax for fluffier pancakes.

instructions.title: Cook
instructions.instruction: Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake and cook until bubbles form on the surface and edges look set, about 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Flip and finish
instructions.instruction: Flip and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes until golden. Repeat with remaining batter, serve warm with butter and maple syrup.

tips: Resting the batter briefly gives noticeably fluffier pancakes.
Wait for bubbles across the whole surface before flipping — it signals the right moment.

substitutions.substitute: Milk + 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar (rested 5 minutes)
substitutions.effect: Very close tang and tenderizing effect to real buttermilk.

storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; reheat in a toaster or skillet. Freezes well up to 1 month.
serving_suggestions: Top with fresh berries and a dusting of powdered sugar.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
description: A rustic, no-lettuce salad of ripe tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and creamy feta dressed simply in olive oil and oregano.

instructions.title: Prep the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Cut tomatoes into wedges, slice cucumber thickly, and thinly slice red onion. Combine in a large bowl.

instructions.title: Add olives
instructions.instruction: Add Kalamata olives to the bowl and toss gently.

instructions.title: Dress
instructions.instruction: Drizzle with olive oil and red wine vinegar, season with salt, and toss gently to coat.

instructions.title: Top with feta
instructions.instruction: Place the feta block whole on top of the salad (traditional style) or crumble over the top. Sprinkle with dried oregano and a final drizzle of olive oil.

tips: Traditionally the feta is served as a whole slab on top, not crumbled — try it for an authentic touch.
Salt the tomatoes lightly a few minutes ahead to draw out extra sweetness.

substitutions.substitute: Firm tofu marinated in lemon and salt
substitutions.effect: Makes the salad vegan with a similar tangy, crumbly texture, though missing feta's distinct sharpness.

storage: Best fresh; if storing, keep dressing separate — refrigerate up to 1 day.
serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread as a light lunch or side.

title: Shepherd's Pie
description: A hearty baked dish of spiced minced lamb and vegetables topped with golden, buttery mashed potato.

instructions.title: Boil the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Boil potato chunks in salted water for 15-18 minutes until fork-tender. Drain and mash with butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions.title: Brown the lamb
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a large pan, add onion and carrot, cook 5 minutes until softened, then add ground lamb and brown for 6-8 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.

instructions.title: Build the filling
instructions.instruction: Stir in tomato paste, stock, and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 15 minutes until thickened. Stir in peas during the last 2 minutes.

instructions.title: Assemble
instructions.instruction: Preheat oven to 200°C/400°F. Spread the lamb filling in a baking dish, then top evenly with mashed potato, spreading to the edges to seal in the filling. Rough up the surface with a fork for extra crispiness. Sprinkle cheese on top if using.

instructions.title: Bake
instructions.instruction: Bake for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden brown and the filling is bubbling at the edges.

tips: Sealing the potato right to the edges of the dish prevents the filling from bubbling over.
Roughing up the mash with a fork before baking creates crispy peaks.

substitutions.effect: Turns the dish into a 'cottage pie' — milder flavor, still hearty and satisfying.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freezes well up to 3 months.
serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed green beans or a simple side salad.

title: Ratatouille
description: A rustic Provençal stewed vegetable dish of eggplant, zucchini, peppers, and tomatoes, simmered in olive oil and herbs.

instructions.title: Sauté the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pot, add onion and garlic, cook for 4-5 minutes until softened.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables in stages
instructions.instruction: Add eggplant and 2 more tbsp oil, cook 5 minutes, then add zucchini and bell peppers. Cook another 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables start to soften.

instructions.title: Add tomatoes and herbs
instructions.instruction: Stir in chopped tomatoes, thyme, and herbes de Provence. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions.title: Simmer
instructions.instruction: Cover and simmer on low heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until all vegetables are tender and the mixture has melded into a thick stew.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Remove thyme sprigs, drizzle with remaining olive oil, and stir in torn fresh basil just before serving.

tips: Cooking the vegetables in stages (rather than all at once) keeps their individual textures from turning to mush.
Ratatouille tastes even better the next day once flavors have melded.

substitutions.effect: Works well out of season with a similar result, slightly softer texture.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; freezes well up to 2 months.
serving_suggestions: Serve as a side to grilled meats, or over crusty bread or rice as a light main.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
description: Slow-simmered chicken with apricots, olives, and warm Moroccan spices in a fragrant, deeply flavored sauce.

instructions.title: Sear the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.

instructions.title: Build the base
instructions.instruction: In the same pot, add onion and garlic, cook 5 minutes until softened. Stir in ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, and cumin, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer
instructions.instruction: Return chicken to the pot, add stock, apricots, and honey. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for 35-40 minutes until chicken is very tender.

instructions.title: Add olives
instructions.instruction: Stir in green olives during the last 10 minutes of cooking.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Taste and adjust salt, garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

tips: A traditional clay tagine pot helps concentrate flavor, but any heavy lidded pot works well.
The sweet-savory balance of apricot and olive is the dish's signature — don't skip either.

substitutions.effect: Slightly different sweetness profile but keeps the same sweet-savory balance.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freezes well up to 2 months.
serving_suggestions: Serve over couscous with extra coriander.

title: Vietnamese Beef Pho
description: A soul-warming Vietnamese noodle soup with a deeply aromatic beef broth, rice noodles, and fresh herbs.

instructions.title: Char the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Char onion and ginger directly over a flame or under a broiler until blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. This deepens the broth's flavor.

instructions.title: Toast the spices
instructions.instruction: Toast star anise, cinnamon, and cloves in a dry pot for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the broth
instructions.instruction: Add beef bones, brisket, charred onion and ginger, and 3 liters of water to the pot. Bring to a boil, skim off scum, then reduce to a gentle simmer.

instructions.title: Simmer low and slow
instructions.instruction: Simmer uncovered for 1.5-2 hours, occasionally skimming fat and impurities, until the broth is rich and aromatic. Season with fish sauce, sugar, and salt.

instructions.title: Prepare noodles and beef
instructions.instruction: Soak rice noodles per package instructions until tender. Strain the broth to remove solids and keep it at a rolling simmer.

instructions.title: Assemble
instructions.instruction: Place noodles in bowls, top with thinly sliced raw beef sirloin, then ladle the very hot broth directly over the top — this gently poaches the raw beef. Serve with bean sprouts, herbs, and lime.

tips: The broth must be at a rolling boil when poured over raw beef to cook it safely and properly.
Charring the onion and ginger is a small step that makes a big flavor difference.

substitutions.effect: Much faster (skip hours of simmering) with a lighter, less complex flavor.

storage: Refrigerate broth and noodles separately up to 3 days; broth freezes well up to 3 months.
serving_suggestions: Serve with hoisin sauce and sriracha on the side for dipping.

title: Classic Banana Bread
description: A moist, tender quick bread packed with ripe mashed banana and a hint of cinnamon.

instructions.title: Preheat and prep
instructions.instruction: Preheat oven to 175°C/350°F and grease a loaf pan.

instructions.title: Mix wet ingredients
instructions.instruction: In a large bowl, mash bananas well, then whisk in melted butter, eggs, and vanilla until combined.

instructions.title: Combine dry ingredients
instructions.instruction: In a separate bowl, whisk flour, sugar, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt.

instructions.title: Fold together
instructions.instruction: Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and fold gently just until no streaks of flour remain — do not overmix. Fold in walnuts if using.

instructions.title: Bake
instructions.instruction: Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan and bake for 50-60 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

instructions.title: Cool
instructions.instruction: Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing.

tips: The riper (more spotted/brown) the bananas, the sweeter and more flavorful the bread.
Overmixing the batter develops gluten and makes the bread dense — mix just until combined.

substitutions.effect: Slightly less rich flavor but an even moister crumb.

storage: Store at room temperature, wrapped, for up to 4 days; freezes well up to 3 months.
serving_suggestions: Delicious on its own or toasted with butter.
